title: Advancing Rehabilitation Through Low Weight Hand Assistive System: Design and Impact Analysis
problem: Individuals with impaired hand function due to stroke, spinal cord injuries, and neuromuscular disorders struggle with daily activities and rehabilitation. Existing assistive devices are often slow and lack real-time feedback.
motivation: Smart assistive devices combining sensor technology, real-time processing, and adaptive actuation provide functional assistance and progressive rehabilitation without burden of conventional approaches.
method: Sensors detect your finger movements and the device instantly processes this data to provide real-time feedback. A motor system (adaptive actuation) amplifies your hand's movements, adjusting its support based on what you're trying to do. A mobile app guides you through therapeutic exercises and interactive games using three control modes: manual assistance, cyclic training, and task-specific routines.
key_novelty: A lightweight hand assistant that gives instant feedback on your movements, automatically adjusts its support while you're using it, and pairs with a mobile app to guide your rehabilitation exercises.
contributions: Smart hand mobility assistive device architecture
Real-time finger movement detection via sensors
Adaptive actuation for subtle movement amplification

metrics.target_users: stroke, spinal cord injury, neuromuscular disorder patients
metrics.evaluation: grip strength, dexterity, overall hand function

limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative performance metrics (improvement percentages, response times); limited technical hardware details; no comparison with competing assistive systems.
